description: While allowing AI for research and translation, the Gujarat High Court policy mandates that all outputs must be verified by a "qualified human officer".
body_lead: The Gujarat High Court introduced a policy to regulate the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in its judicial and administrative functions Saturday. Acknowledging “rapid technological advancement” and the influx of “techno-savvy judicial officers,” the policy prohibits the application of AI in judicial decision-making, evaluating evidence or drafting substantive orders. While it permits judges and court staff to use AI as a controlled administrative and research aid – such as for translating documents, checking grammar and managing cause lists- it mandates human oversight.
